sources.note: This is the only published work by the p.c. source named by Glottolog, but it describes the SPOKEN Yanomama of Papiu (ISO wca, Glottolog Yanomámi yano1262), not the sign language. a full-text search for stress/accent both full-text parts (779 pp.) for sign language/signed/deaf/gesture/Libras returns zero relevant hits: the sign language is not mentioned. For the spoken language, §2.5 'Word and prosodic stress' (p. 52, PDF p. 72) says stress is not distinctive and tends to fall on the penultimate syllable, with three noted exceptions (certain enclitics attract final stress) and a prosodic role…
